_provenance.derived_from: 84 AS Business 9609 mark schemes (Papers 1 and 2), 2020-2025. Papers 3 and 4 are A Level and excluded.
_provenance.evidence_window: Answer shapes use 2023 onward only. The mark schemes changed format in 2023 - from a plain list of mark bands to a grid that attributes every mark to an assessment objective - and the paper structure from 2023 matches the current syllabus. 2020-2022 are used only to record what the current papers no longer ask.
_provenance.validation: Printed totals reconcile to the syllabus: Paper 1 prints 60 (Section A 4 x 5 + Section B 2 x 20, candidate answers one essay, for 40); Paper 2 prints 60 (two compulsory questions of 30, each in six parts: 1 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 8 + 12).
_provenance.derivation_policy: structure only. No mark-scheme wording is reproduced in learner-facing output.

9609.subject: Cambridge International AS Level Business

paper_architecture.P1: Section A: Q1-Q3 each Define 2 + Explain 3; Q4 Analyse 5. Section B: two essays of Analyse 8 + Evaluate 12, one answered.
paper_architecture.P2: Two compulsory case questions, each: Identify 1, Explain 3, Calculate 3, Explain 3, Analyse 8, Evaluate 12 = 30.

shapes.verified: 1 mark, AO1. No grid is printed for a one-mark part.
shapes.guard: Tautological or vague answers are refused: restating the term in the stem earns nothing.

shapes.verified: AO split read off the mark scheme’s own AO grid on 49 of 63 questions carrying one; 49 of 49 agree.
shapes.guard: An example is not a definition.

shape: that point applied to a business context: AO2 2 marks for developed application, 1 for limited
shapes.verified: AO split read off the mark scheme’s own AO grid on 121 of 143 questions carrying one; 121 of 121 agree.
shapes.note: The commonest part on both AS papers. One point, taken all the way into a context - not two points.

shape: formula with the figures substituted: 1 mark
shapes.verified: Read from the mark schemes’ own step marking; a correct final answer alone earns all three. Own-figure rule applies.
shapes.note: Always introduced by "Refer to lines..." or "Refer to Table/Fig...": the figures come from the stimulus.

shapes.verified: AO split read off the mark scheme’s own AO grid on 14 of 20 questions carrying one; 14 of 14 agree.
shapes.note: Paper 1 Section A, question 4: a single five-mark part.

shape: each developed into connected causes, impacts or consequences: AO3 4
shapes.verified: AO split read off the mark scheme’s own AO grid on 49 of 82 questions carrying one; 49 of 49 agree.
shapes.bands_top: 3-4 marks of AO3 for developed analysis that identifies connections between causes, impacts and/or consequences of two points.
shapes.note: Paper 1 Section B part (a) and Paper 2 part (c).

shape: evaluation: AO4 6 - a developed judgement in context
shapes.verified: AO split read off the mark scheme’s own AO grid on 43 of 59 questions carrying one; 43 of 43 agree.
shapes.bands_top: 5-6 marks of AO4 for developed evaluation in context: a developed judgement or conclusion that follows from the argument.
shapes.note: Half the marks are evaluation. The final part of every Paper 2 question and of every Paper 1 essay.

retired_forms.Discuss: 46 questions 2020-2022, none from 2023. Not in the current syllabus table.
retired_forms.Recommend: 19 questions 2020-2022, none from 2023. Not in the current syllabus table.
retired_forms.Evaluate at 11 marks: 16 questions 2020-2022; from 2023 the final part is 12 marks.

refusals: a tautological answer that restates the term in the question earns nothing
a vague answer is refused even when it is not wrong
an example is not a definition
two points where one was asked for are not both credited; one point taken into context is
a judgement that does not follow from the argument before it is not developed evaluation
